preview_en:
Netherlands and Germany renew their fierce rivalry in this UEFA Nations League (UNL) opener, with both sides beginning new eras following World Cup exits at the first knockout stage.

Match News and Current Form

Spanish legend Xavi succeeded Ronald Koeman as manager after the Netherlands were knocked out of the World Cup by Morocco, and he’s wasted no time stamping his authority on the squad, with the omission of the nation’s record scorer Memphis Depay his most eye-catching decision. He'll be looking to retain some of the steel his predecessor instilled though, as the Oranje have only lost once in regulation time across their last 20 matches (W11, D8). They’ve won exactly half of their UNL fixtures (W12, D9, L3) but fell short of a third appearance in the semi-finals from four attempts in 2024/25 when they were eliminated in the quarter-finals, while the Dutch have been beaten at home just once since October 2023 (W11, D4).

Jürgen Klopp returns to management for the first time since leaving Liverpool, taking over from Julian Nagelsmann after Germany’s embarrassing World Cup exit to Paraguay. A new era begins for the 2024/25 UNL semi-finalists with a whopping 43 players called up, 15 of them uncapped, across two squads for these four UNL games. After closing their World Cup poorly (L2), Germany could go three games without a win for the first time since a run of four ending in September 2025, although they’ll take encouragement from losing only one of their last nine away matches against European opponents (W6, D2).

Head-to-Head History

Germany have the better overall H2H record (W18, D18, L12) and have lost just one of the last seven meetings (W3, D3). Two of the four previous UNL H2Hs finished 2-2 (W1, L1).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Netherlands’ last five games saw both teams score after half-time.

Netherlands conceded exactly once in each of their last four home matches.

There was at least one goal in each half of Germany’s last nine games.

Germany won the corner count in seven of their last nine fixtures.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Netherlands’ Brian Brobbey comes into this fixture after netting a hat-trick for Sunderland against Manchester City at the weekend, and two of his three international goalscoring outings saw him net the match opener. Jamal Musiala has three goal contributions across his last three games for Bayern Munich (G2, A1) while Germany have never lost a game he’s scored in (W9, D1).

Justin Kluivert and Donyell Malen pulled out of the Netherlands’ squad due to injuries, while Brajan Gruda withdrew from Germany’s squad.

Betting Analysis

With half of these teams’ previous UNL H2Hs finishing level and both now under new management, backing another draw has plenty of appeal.

Author: John Pennington
